must_cover: What the part is: the Quantro QT1190, an analog temperature sensor in a 5-lead SOT-23 package whose output voltage is proportional to temperature (10 mV per degree C, 500 mV at 0 degrees C), no calibration needed

Headline specs: supply 2.7 V to 5.5 V, quiescent current 12 uA typical (20 uA max), shutdown current 0.1 uA typical, operating range -40 to +125 degrees C, accuracy 0.5 degrees C typical at 25 degrees C
Pinout: five pins, 1 VS, 2 GND, 3 SHDN (active low, tie to VS for normal operation), 4 NC, 5 VOUT; pin 1 is marked with a dot, pins 1 to 3 on the bottom edge of the top view
Absolute maximum ratings are stress limits, not operating conditions: supply -0.3 V to 6.0 V, storage -65 to 150 degrees C, junction 150 degrees C, ESD 2000 V, soldering 260 degrees C for 10 s

Electrical characteristics are given as min / typ / max at VS = 3.3 V and 25 degrees C; guaranteed limits are the min and max columns, typical values are information only (scale factor 9.9 / 10.0 / 10.1 mV per degree C; error 0.5 typ and 2.0 max for grade A, 1.0 max for grade B)
The characteristic curve is a straight line: 100 mV at -40 degrees C, 500 mV at 0, 750 mV at 25, 1750 mV at 125 degrees C; to read a temperature subtract 500 mV and divide by 10 mV per degree C
Typical application: 100 nF bypass capacitor at VS, SHDN tied to VS, RC filter with 1 kOhm and 1 nF between VOUT and the ADC input
Ordering information: three models (QT1190AKS-R7, QT1190AKS-RL, QT1190BKS-R7) plus an evaluation board; grade B is the tighter accuracy
units: nF (bypass is 100 nF; filter capacitor is 1 nF, state both)
figures: Figure 1 (page 1): top view of the SOT-23-5 package with pins numbered 1, 2, 3 on the bottom edge and 5, 4 on the top edge, names VS, GND, SHDN below and VOUT, NC above; the dot at the lower left marks pin 1. Point at pin 5 (VOUT) and pin 1 (VS) and read the pin function table next to it
Pin function table (page 1, no caption): Pin / Name / Description for the five pins
Table 1 'Absolute maximum ratings' (page 1, captioned): parameter, symbol, rating for nine items

Table 2 'Electrical characteristics' (page 2, captioned): parameter, test conditions, min, typ, max, unit, in three groups Accuracy, Output and Power supply; empty cells mean there is no value in that column; point at the scale factor row (9.9 / 10.0 / 10.1) and the quiescent current row (12 typ, 20 max)

Figure 2 (page 2): pgfplots curve of output voltage (mV, 0 to 1750) versus temperature (-40 to 125 degrees C); a straight line through 100, 300, 500, 750, 1000, 1350, 1550, 1750 mV; the annotations mark 500 mV at 0 degrees C and 750 mV at 25 degrees C
Figure 3 (page 3): circuit with supply VS = 3.3 V, 100 nF capacitor C1 to ground, QT1190 with SHDN tied to VS, GND, and VOUT through RF = 1 kOhm to the ADC input with CF = 1 nF to ground
Ordering information table (page 3, no caption): model, accuracy, package, marking, packing
pitfalls: Do not treat typical values as guaranteed limits; only min and max are guaranteed
Do not present the absolute maximum ratings as operating conditions (operating supply is 2.7 V to 5.5 V, not up to 6.0 V)
Do not mix up pin numbers and names (pin 3 is SHDN, pin 5 is VOUT, pin 4 is NC) or the top-view orientation
Do not invent numbers that are not in the datasheet, such as an accuracy figure for grade B over the full temperature range or a price
Do not give a design recommendation beyond what the application section says (100 nF close to the supply pin, SHDN at the supply voltage, RC filter at the output)
Do not confuse the 10 mV/degC scale factor with the 0.5 degC accuracy; one is a slope, the other an error band
